$comment: The retry decision both SDKs make, as data. Each outcome row gives, per route class (routes.json), `retry` or `raise`. A retry is bounded by defaults.json `max_retries` and waits per its `backoff`, unless a Retry-After of at most `retry_after_cap_seconds` is present, which wins. Rows are checked in order and the first match decides; a row matches on its `network` outcomes, its `status` codes, or its `codes` (the problem document's `code`), and, where it says so, on whether the answer's Retry-After is `within_cap` or `beyond_cap` (none counts as within). A `codes` row names answers whose code says a repeat cannot help although their status is otherwise retried; it comes before every row matching those codes' statuses. Normative: an SDK whose decision differs from this table has a bug. The billing facts it rests on (dsp-backend src/dsp/features/billing/meter.py): a billed call is charged after its work succeeds, as the last step that can fail, so any error answer means nothing was charged; but a first page of search or similar opens a new paid session, so a billed request that may have reached the server without an answer is never repeated.

outcomes.description: The request provably never reached the server: connection refused, DNS failure, connect timeout.
The request may have been processed: read timeout, connection reset after send, a 502 from a proxy in front of the server, or a 408 from one that gave up waiting for the server.
notes: billed: the error carries reached_server=True (Python) / reachedServer: true (JS), and its message says the call may have been charged.
keyed: the retry resends the same Idempotency-Key, so the server recognises the repeat.

outcomes.description: Answers whose code says a repeat cannot help, though their status is otherwise retried. 429 quota.concurrency_exceeded: the credential already has as many agent runs going as it may, and a run takes minutes, so its Retry-After rarely frees a slot; follow or cancel a run instead. 503 credits.refused: the credit ledger refused to hold for this work, nothing ran, and only support can change it. Raised at once, never slept on.
429 with a Retry-After of at most retry_after_cap_seconds, or none.
429 with a Retry-After above retry_after_cap_seconds. Raised at once with the value attached; never slept through.
Deterministic answers: repeating the request cannot change them.
500. A billed call is charged only as its last step, so its error answer was not charged and a retry cannot pay twice; a `once` call may have taken effect, so it is raised.
503 and 504: the work was refused or abandoned before any charge, so a retry cannot pay twice. A 503 carries Retry-After (1 s, or 30 s for credits.unavailable), which is honoured.
